title: Photography
text:
As a wizard and scholar of Middle-earth, I have been studying the magic of the natural world for centuries. Through my self-portraits, I aim to capture the essence of my own being and reflect on my own journey through time. Each photograph is a reflection of my own experiences and emotions. Through my photography, I hope to offer a glimpse into my life as a scholar and adventurer, and inspire others to reflect on their own journeys through the world.

title: Projects
text:
arXiv Preprint | Code
Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

section: The History of the War of the Ring
text:
The History of the War of the Ring

arXiv Preprint | Code
I am creating a comprehensive and detailed history of the conflict that goes beyond the surface-level events. By gathering information from a variety of sources, including my own memories, written accounts, and oral histories, I hope to shed new light on this important period in Middle-earth’s history and provide valuable insights into the motivations and actions of the various players involved.

Welcome to my website!
Hi, my name is Grayson Porter Shanks. I am in my 4th year at Case Western Reserve University as Biochemistry B.S. and mathematics minor undergraduate candidate. I have been involved on campus by being the co-President of Ensemble (French Club), where we create a welcoming environment for those that want to practice or learn French both as a language and or as a culture. I am thankful to be a member of CWRU EMS, which is a collegiate EMS service, for nearly 4 years at this point. I have served as the head driver trainer, and I aim to always encourage others and to educate our new clinical members as they find their way in becoming an EMT.
Apart from my involvement in clubs, I volunteer with the Center for Civic Engagement and Learning as a student leader. We have been able to help prepare high schoolers for taking their ACT, provide companionship for those in retirement homes, as well as help tutor elementary to middle schoolers in their homework ranging from math to history.
I also engage in basic science research through the Dr. Levine laboratory. Learn more by accessing the link above. In the lab, I have been exploring the effects of a microbial byproduct, acrolein, and its effect on barrier integrity in the colon.
When I am not doing homework, or in lab, or something else, I really enjoy my time baking and cooking. My favorite thing to bake is a yule log around Christmas. I also enjoy going to concerts such as Kendrick Lamar, Isaiah Rashad, Zach Bryan, Deftones.
It is my goal to apply to medical school and become a physician. My current plan after I graduate is to move to North Carolina and to work in a hospital for my two gap years until I apply in Spring 2028 and matriculate Fall 2029.
If you are interesting in reaching out to me for whatever reason, please reach out contact me.
Have a great day!
